contradicting_evidence: The completed hourly candle offers a near-term upside signal: BTC rose approximately 0.67% and ETH 0.55%, with taker-buy quote shares near 60% and 58%.
The 24h breadth snapshot offers an opposing downside signal: only 13 of 100 constituents advanced, while BTC and ETH were down approximately 5.90% and 7.72%.
The latest settled ETF session was positive for both assets, opposing an uninterrupted selling-pressure interpretation.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A rebound extension and a failed-rebound retest are both credible; the supplied evidence does not distinguish them sufficiently for a net 12h direction. BTC looks firmer than ETH in the observed repair, but broad participation has not confirmed that repair. The gap between observation and issuance further weakens the short-horizon inference.
falsification_conditions: The no-edge assessment would resolve toward UP if subsequent completed hours sustain price gains with persistent spot buying, improving ETH/BTC and broader positive participation.
It would resolve toward DOWN if both assets lose the observed repair while selling pressure and weak participation persist.
A BTC-only extension without improving ETH/BTC or breadth would not establish broad-market upside.
missing_evidence: Price and order-flow developments between the 10:00 UTC candle completion and issuance.
Repeated hourly observations showing whether spot demand persists rather than appearing in a single candle or trade sample.
A refreshed breadth observation measuring participation during the rebound rather than the preceding 24h decline.
supporting_evidence: The evidence spans opposing time windows: a positive completed hour sits inside a sharply negative 24h snapshot, so stabilization cannot be treated as continuation.
BTC price rose while open interest declined approximately 0.36%, consistent with covering or position reduction rather than confirmed fresh risk-taking.
ETH price and open interest rose together, but ETH/BTC fell approximately 0.10% during the hour and closed at its observed hourly low.

BTC's sampled order-book imbalance was positive, whereas ETH's was negative; both had positive sampled taker imbalance. These are mixed, venue-specific observations rather than persistent market-wide confirmation.
